s: Who was the greatest king of Chalukya dynasty?
x: Pulakesin - II was the most capable and powerful ruler of Chalukyas, who ruled from 610 to 642 AD. Aihole inscription provides the saga of his achievements.

s: The Sanskrit poet and dramatist Kalidasa finds a mention in –
x: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II, composed by Ravikirti, names Kalidasa and Bharavi, claiming fame like theirs. The other inscriptions listed do not mention Kalidasa.

s: The name of poet Kalidasa is mentioned in the:
x: Aihole inscription is an authentic source for Pulakesin - II history. It is engraved in Sanskrit and southern Brahmi language and was written by Ravikirti. At the end of commendation, the author claimed that he had gained fame like Kalidasa and Bharavi by writing this. Thus, the name of poet Kalidasa is mentioned in the Aihole inscription.

s: Which inscription of Pulakesi-II mentions Mangalagiri as Mangalapura?
x:
The Kopparam Inscription of Pulakesi II, the famous Chalukya ruler of Badami, refers to Mangalagiri by its ancient name "Mangalapura." The inscription is an important historical source for studying the Chalukya expansion into the Andhra region and provides valuable information regarding political geography and place names of the period. The identification of Mangalagiri as Mangalapura is frequently asked in APPSC examinations. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).

• Inscription – Kopparam Inscription
• Ancient name of Mangalagiri – Mangalapura
• Ruler – Pulakesi II
